grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, milk, natural yoghurt, honey, fresh fruit, lemon, cinnamon and pumpkin seeds are all ordinary kitchen staples with no factory-made products.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item, and blueberries and peaches are at their cheapest in July.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, a grater for the zest and a fork, with simple stirring and crushing.

works.reason: 200g oats to 300ml milk and 200g yoghurt soaked overnight gives a sensible bircher for four, with enough fruit, sweetness and lemon to taste good.

honest_times.reason: Ten minutes covers zesting, stirring, crushing berries and slicing two peaches, and the 480 minutes is the overnight soak given in the time note.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, the names match their ids, and the lemon is used as zest with nothing unlisted brought in.

seasonal_feel.reason: A cold fruit bircher suits a July morning, and the blueberries are both stirred through and piled on top, so they are clearly the point.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oats, yoghurt, plenty of fruit and seeds make a filling, wholesome breakfast with only a little honey.
